text:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing divergent KV-cache rotation/eviction behavior across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private after the latest kernel-selector + batching heuristics tweak. Hosted looks stable, Dedicated shows steady fragmentation creep, Private (on-prem) exhibits memory growth over long contexts.
Maria: Can you paste the short profiler snapshot & numbers? :eyes:
Alex: Quick profiler summary from same synthetic run (seq=4096, batch=8):
```
KV slots: total=1.2M used=0.92M free=280k
Hosted: frag=8.2% avg_reuse=430 tokens
Dedicated: frag=24.7% avg_reuse=210 tokens
Private-onprem: frag=31.5% avg_reuse=95 tokens
Evict ops/s: hosted=450 dedicated=670 private=980
Last kernel selected: attention-opt-v3 (bigger slice, TF32 path)
```
Sam: That smells like allocation pattern change from the new kernel chunking. Dedicated still uses jemalloc with tuned arenas; Private machines have older drivers and pinned allocations sometimes delayed. Any differences in hugepages/madvise?
Alex: Yep — Private boxes have transparent hugepages disabled but also an older CUDA driver that defers GPU-side free/unmap in certain codepaths. Combined with larger batch token window we increase stride so reuse drops and eviction rotates more aggressively -> fragmentation climbs.
Jonah: Can you spell out repro steps so infra can run the same? Also, check slab/page alignment on on-prem GPUs — they often prefer 2MB alignment.
Sam: Repro snippet we used:
```
# synthetic perf runner
./perf_runner --model llama2-70b --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kv-rotation=auto --max_batch_tokens=4096 --profiling=kv
```
Alex: Ran that on Hosted, Dedicated, Private (same binary, different infra). Flame links: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/1806001111-hosted  , https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/1806001111-dedicated , https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/1806001111-private
ci-bot: perf job 1806001111 finished — hosted: PASS, dedicated: REGRESSION (+3.2% mem), private: REGRESSION (+9.1% mem). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1806001111/log
Maria: Short-term mitigations to try: 1) lower max_batch_tokens to 2048 for Dedicated/Private, 2) change KV rotation policy from LRU -> CLOCK (less aggressive churn), 3) enable immediate page unmap on free if driver supports it.
Alex: I'll run the 2048 and CLOCK experiments on canary pools this afternoon and report numbers. Expect a canary in ~4h. :thumbsup:
Jonah: Also add telemetry tag for kernel-selector decisions + kv-alloc metadata (slice size, alignment) so Console can correlate regressions to kernel picks.
Sam: Agreed. If Private can't be fixed without driver updates, we should add a documented prerequisite for Private (CUDA/driver minimums) and a runtime fallback that forces smaller slice/kernel.
Alex: Will try mitigations and post results back here. Thanks — will follow up with graphs and config diffs. :pray:
